localBiteReport: Note: The most recent angler catch reports found for Choctawhatchee Bay are from June–July 2026 — roughly 2 to 3 months old — so treat these as background context rather than a live bite update. That said, the picture is consistent: speckled trout have been the standout inshore species, scattered across the bay's grass flats and biting actively, with bull redfish (some pushing 25+ lbs) also showing well around the bay's channels and structure. Anglers fishing the Santa Rosa Beach and West Bay areas reported solid mixed bags of trout and slot reds, and a 43-lb black drum was landed on a West Bay trip in late June. Water temperature today at this location is 87°F. September typically marks the beginning of the fall transition, which historically improves both redfish and trout action on Choctawhatchee Bay as bait schools up and fish begin staging near creek mouths and channel edges.
